title: RANT : AppleCare "Tech Support"
description: This is a rant video about Apple. If you don't like rant videos, click the back button ... QUICK.

asr.full_text: Alright this video is gonna be a rant so if you don't want to hear a rant turn the channel because it's about to happen I am absolutely furious right now with Apple they ever since Steve Jobs died they have been going downhill in my opinion I've given them a lots and lots of grace and patience and everything but they keep doing everything wrong and this ticks me off because I want them to succeed. I want to continue to be an Apple fanboy, but it's just not turning out that way. My recent example is kind of why I'm making this video. There's two examples and they follow the same pattern, and it's a very frustrating pattern. The pattern is this. Apple tech support has three things that they do. Reboot, replace, sorry, reboot, restore, replace. That's their whole process. Where in there did they actually figure out what caused the issue and fix it? There isn't any because as soon as you restore it and if the issue is gone, that's it. That's, you can't tell what was the problem before if it's already fixed. Same with replacing the device. So I had an iPhone. It kept rebooting randomly. They said, oh, can you reboot it? Well, sure. I'll appease them and reboot it still have the same issue okay well let's restore the software which is a huge pain even with iCloud back up it still takes a bunch of time so I restore it just to follow their procedure and it still does it okay sir it sounds like a hardware issue let's replace it okay I get a new iPhone which is great I replace it. Okay i get a new iphone, which is great i'm glad that they give me a new iphone same issue so now what? nobody has any idea what was actually causing the issue we've restored it, we've rebooted it, we've replaced it and it's still happening nobody looks into it any deeper than that so now i'm having an issue on my mac. I have an iMac. Top of the line 5k iMac decked out. Randomly the notification center there's a bunch notifications listed when I click the clear all button randomly they just won't do anything, none of the notifications clear. So I've been putting up with it manually closing each notification but I decided today I'm gonna call apple tech support. I've been putting up with it and manually closing each notification, but I decided today I'm going to call Apple Tech Support. I've got AppleCare on this iMac. I might as well use it. So I call them up, and what do they say? Let's reboot the computer. Okay, well, that didn't fix it. Okay, sir, now I want you to restore the computer. Do you get what restoring an iMac is? I mean, I'm running a web development company. I've got everything set up exactly how I need it, and now I've got to restore it. And there's backups and things like that, but nothing is exactly like you left it. So now they just want me to restore it. And they said, and if the restore doesn't work, then we'll just give you a new iMac. I don't want a new iMac. I want you, Apple, to look into the issue, the cause of the issue and fix the cause of the issue! You used to be such a reliable computer, it just worked everything just worked, yes its technology there's a little glitches here and there but for the most part it just worked and over the last few years, that hasn't been the case. On my iPhone, on my Macs, I have multiple Macs. They all have these weird little glitchy issues, and all they want you to do is reboot, restore and replace. It doesn't feel like they're looking into the root cause of the issue. Are there not any logs you can look at? Or diagnostics you can run to see what is causing this issue so that we can fix it in the next version? That's all I want. I don't even want you to fix it right now. You've got to go through the whole chain of command for fixing a software glitch. But let's find the root cause of the issue and fix it instead of just replacing it. So, that's my rant. I have no idea what kind of reaction this is gonna get that's just how I feel like I said huge Apple fanboy but this is getting ridiculous and I don't even want to call in and talk to Apple care anymore because that's the process they're gonna follow and ultimately it's just gonna end up nobody knows what actually was the cause of the issue but I have a new device so that's it talk to you later

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents a personal rant criticizing repeated device rebooting, restoring, or replacement without identifying the underlying cause. Its central message requests that Apple investigate those causes, rather than soliciting payment, credentials, or financial participation.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary subject is an ordinary consumer technology service and related devices: the speaker discusses Apple technical support, AppleCare, an iPhone, and Macs in the context of troubleshooting and replacement.

evidence.observation: The speaker describes Apple technical support as repeatedly using reboot, restore, and replacement procedures.
evidence.quote: Apple tech support has three things that they do. Reboot, replace, sorry, reboot, restore, replace.

evidence.observation: The speaker refers to using AppleCare service coverage for the iMac.
evidence.quote: I've got AppleCare on this iMac. I might as well use it.

evidence.observation: The speaker discusses reported issues involving an iPhone and multiple Mac computers.
evidence.quote: On my iPhone, on my Macs, I have multiple Macs.

evidence.observation: The speaker criticizes Apple support for not investigating the underlying cause of the reported device issues.
evidence.quote: It doesn't feel like they're looking into the root cause of the issue.
